hints: A larger filled square ending at a cell requires three smaller neighboring squares.
Add the largest valid size at each cell to the count for its letter.
analogy: Grow solid squares from their bottom-right corner.
example: In a 2 by 2 grid of A, there are four size-one squares and one size-two square, for 5.
algorithm: For each cell, set dp to 1. If its top, left and top-left neighbors exist and all have the same letter as the cell, set dp to 1 plus the minimum of those three neighbors? dp values. Add dp to the total for this cell?s letter. Use two rows of dp.
correctness: A square of side s>1 is filled exactly when its three overlapping side-(s-1) squares ending above, left and diagonally above-left are filled with the same letter. Thus dp counts exactly the possible sizes ending at the cell, and every square has one bottom-right corner.
complexity: For an n by n grid, time is O(n^2) and extra space O(n), apart from the input grid.
